name: Nasdaq.com news feeds and articles
description: Nasdaq.com's public news surfaces: ticker news, press releases, market-wide and topic feeds (JSON), the RSS feeds that carry publish times, and the full text and exact publish instant of a Nasdaq article or press release page.

tools.name: Article
tools.description: Full text and the exact publish time of a story listed by any feed function. Costs one ~180 KB page fetch.

options.name: url
options.about: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/{slug} or https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/{slug}, as returned in `items[].url`.

response.about: One Nasdaq.com story page (`/articles/{slug}` or `/press-release/{slug}`): title, publisher and author from the page's JSON-LD, the exact publish instant as RFC 3339 UTC (JSON-LD datePublished on articles; the `Published` stamp with its EDT/EST zone on press releases), the topic and quote symbols from Nasdaq's CMS meta tags, and the body paragraphs from the Mercury text block. Only nasdaq.com URLs are accepted; third-party publisher pages are out of scope. A slug Nasdaq does not know is `not_found`.

fields.name: author
fields.about: JSON-LD author name (for syndicated stories Nasdaq puts the publisher here).

fields.name: body_text
fields.about: `paragraphs` joined by blank lines.

fields.name: final_url
fields.about: The URL that answered after redirects.

fields.name: modified_at
fields.about: JSON-LD dateModified as UTC; null when absent.

fields.name: paragraphs
fields.about: Body text blocks in page order (paragraphs, headings, list items).

fields.name: published_at
fields.about: RFC 3339 UTC. Articles: JSON-LD datePublished (`Mon, 09/21/2026 - 18:35`, a UTC wall clock; verified against the RSS epoch). Press releases: the page's `Published` stamp (`Sep 9, 2026 2:15pm EDT`) converted from its stated zone. Null only when the page states neither.

fields.name: published_label
fields.about: The human-readable stamp as the page shows it, e.g. `September 21, 2026 - 02:35 pm EDT`.

fields.name: publisher
fields.about: Syndication source from the page's digitalData (`The Motley Fool`); null when the page names none (press releases).

fields.name: quote_symbols
fields.about: Symbols from the CMS quoteSymbol meta tags, upper-cased, de-duplicated.

fields.name: topic
fields.about: Nasdaq CMS topic tag (`markets`); null when absent.

fields.name: url
fields.about: The URL as requested.

response.body_text:
Key Points

It's been 10 years since Berkshire Hathaway first invested in Apple stock.

It has been the company's largest holding since 2017.

The Apple position encompasses many of Buffett's investing tenets.

Of all the great investments that former Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA) (NYSE: BRKB) CEO Warren Buffett made over the years, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) might have been his best.

Up until his first investment in Apple in 2016, or perhaps with a position he opened in International Business Machines (NYSE: IBM) in 2011, Buffett had been reluctant to invest in technology stocks because he said he didn't fully understand them.

Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"-the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But he soon understood Apple enough to make it his largest holding and best investment. Over the years, Berkshire has made more than $100 billion on Apple stock, Buffett told CNBC back in July of this year.

Former Berkshire Hathaway CEO Warren Buffett. Image source: The Motley Fool.

Best business in the world

Back in 2020 on CNBC, Buffett called Apple "probably the best business I know in the world," adding that he doesn't think of Apple as a stock. "I think of it as our third business." That would be a third business along with insurance and railroads.

That first investment in Apple stock was 9.8 million shares in the first quarter of 2016, when the stock traded at about $25 per share. It was just the beginning of Berkshire Hathaway's commitment to Apple, which Buffett himself discussed at the 2026 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder meeting back in May.

"About 10 years ago, we made a commitment to essentially move 10% of the total resources of Berkshire Hathaway. We turned it over to another person who was not that well known at the time, and we did that by spending roughly $35 billion buying stock in Apple Corp," Buffett said. "I would like to report that 10 years later, several things have happened. One is that the $35 billion -- counting dividends, realized appreciation, and unrealized appreciation -- has turned into $185 billion pretax."

Apple became Berkshire's largest holding by the end of 2017, representing about 15% of the total portfolio. Six years later, by the end of 2023, Berkshire had amassed a $174 billion investment in Apple, which made up a staggering 50% of its $347 billion portfolio.

After that, Buffett began paring back Berkshire Hathaway's Apple position. Part of it was surely profit-taking, but he also said in a recent interview that he was wary about having one stock take up 50% of the portfolio. Apple is still Berkshire's largest position, but it's "only" a $66 billion investment, making up 22% of the total portfolio.

The perfect Buffett investment

There are key takeaways from Berkshire's long-term commitment to Apple that illuminate some of Buffett's investing tenets. One is to buy great businesses at fair prices. In early 2016, Apple stock had slumped and was trading at a deep discount, at just 10 times earnings, its lowest valuation in 10 years.

It also represents Buffett's belief in investing in companies with strong leadership and management -- in this case, former Apple CEO Tim Cook. "When we made our investment and turned over 10% of Berkshire's resources, we were turning it over to Tim. As I say, he has turned that into $185 billion pretax," Buffett said at the shareholder meeting. "I think it's appropriate if Tim Cook would take a bow and our shareholders would say thanks to him."

Further, Apple had, and has, the kind of industry leadership and competitive moat that sets it up for long-term success. And of course, the 10-plus year investment in Apple shows the value of holding on to a great investment for the long term, even though Buffett himself recently admitted that he might have sold too soon on Apple.

But overall, Berkshire's investment in Apple isn't just a great example of the benefits of long-term investing. It also represents, perhaps, the perfect Buffett investment -- the culmination of everything he looks for in a stock.

Should you buy stock in Apple right now?

Before you buy stock in Apple, consider this:

The Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now… and Apple wasn’t one of them. The 10 stocks that made the cut could produce monster returns in the coming years.

Consider when Netflix made this list on December 17, 2004... if you invested $1,000 at the time of our recommendation, you’d have $387,158!* Or when Nvidia made this list on April 15, 2005... if you invested $1,000 at the time of our recommendation, you’d have $1,365,749!*

Now, it’s worth noting Stock Advisor’s total average return is 932% - a market-crushing outperformance compared to 211% for the S&P 500. Don't miss the latest top 10 list, available with Stock Advisor, and join an investing community built by individual investors for individual investors.

See the 10 stocks »

*Stock Advisor returns as of September 21, 2026.

Dave Kovaleski has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Apple, Berkshire Hathaway, and International Business Machines. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

tools.name: Feed
tools.description: Publish times for the newest stories on a ticker or topic in one request. For older stories or more than 15 rows use `ticker_news` / `topic_news` and `article`.

options.name: category
options.about: Nasdaq topic name as shown in `primary_topic` (Markets, Stocks, Technology, Investing). Case-sensitive as Nasdaq spells it. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 &'\-]*$.

options.name: symbol
options.about: Exchange ticker as Nasdaq spells it (AAPL, BRK.B, SPY). Case-insensitive. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.\-]{0,9}$.

response.about: Nasdaq's RSS feed (`/feed/rssoutbound`) for one ticker, one topic category, or the whole site: the 15 newest articles, each with its exact publish instant (`published_at`, RFC 3339 UTC from pubDate, cross-checked against the guid epoch), publisher, topic, tagged tickers and teaser. This is the only Nasdaq list surface that carries a time of day. It lists articles only, never press releases. An unknown ticker or category is `not_found` (Nasdaq would silently answer the site-wide feed; that fallback is detected).

fields.name: published_at
fields.about: pubDate, RFC 3339 UTC.

fields.name: published_at_epoch
fields.about: Unix seconds from the guid `?time=` parameter; equals `published_at`.

fields.name: publisher
fields.about: dc:creator; null when absent.

fields.name: tickers
fields.about: nasdaq:tickers, upper-cased, de-duplicated, Nasdaq's order.

fields.name: topic
fields.about: RSS category; null when absent.

tools.name: Latest headlines
tools.description: What is being published right now across the market, with no ticker or topic filter.

options.name: limit
options.about: Rows per page (1-200).

options.name: offset
options.about: Rows to skip. Nasdaq serves at most 500 rows per feed and its edge denies deeper offsets, so 490 is the last usable offset; `next_offset` from the previous page is the safe value.

options.name: with_publish_times
options.about: Also fetch the matching RSS feed (one extra request) and copy its pubDate into `published_at` for the stories it lists (the 15 newest). Set false to save the request.

response.about: Nasdaq.com's market-wide latest-news feed (`latestnews`), newest first across every syndicated publisher, up to 500 rows deep. Rows carry Nasdaq's calendar day and `ago` label plus `published_at` (RFC 3339 UTC) for the stories the default RSS feed lists (its 15 newest).

fields.name: ago
fields.about: Nasdaq's relative label (`55 minutes ago`, `7 days ago`, or a date for older items) computed on Nasdaq's server at fetch time. It is a different clock from `published_date` and is not a publish time; see `observed_at_ms` for when it was read.

fields.name: description
fields.about: Teaser text; null when empty.

fields.name: id
fields.about: Nasdaq CMS node id; stable per story.

fields.name: kind
fields.about: From the URL family: /articles/, /press-release/, /videos/.

fields.name: primary_symbol
fields.about: Nasdaq's `primarysymbol`, upper-cased. Nasdaq fills it only for stories it files under one company; empty for most syndicated market wraps.

fields.name: primary_topic
fields.about: Topic name from `primarytopic` (Markets, Stocks, Technology...).

fields.name: primary_topic_id
fields.about: Topic term id from `primarytopic`; input for `topic_news`.

fields.name: published_at
fields.about: Publish instant, RFC 3339 UTC, taken from the matching Nasdaq RSS feed item (pubDate) when this story is among that feed's 15 newest items. Null otherwise; `article` returns the instant for any story.

fields.name: published_at_source
fields.about: `rss` when `published_at` came from the RSS feed; null when `published_at` is null.

fields.name: published_date
fields.about: Calendar day from Nasdaq's `created` field (US-Eastern day; the feed carries no time of day). Null when Nasdaq sends none.

fields.name: published_label
fields.about: Nasdaq's `created` text verbatim, e.g. `Sep 21, 2026`.

fields.name: publisher
fields.about: Syndication source as Nasdaq labels it (Zacks, The Motley Fool, Barchart, RTTNews...). Null when Nasdaq sends an empty string (most press releases).

fields.name: related_symbols
fields.about: Every symbol Nasdaq tagged on the story, upper-cased, in Nasdaq's order.

fields.name: url
fields.about: Absolute www.nasdaq.com URL of the story; pass it to `article` for the full text and the exact publish time.

tools.name: Ticker news
tools.description: Latest third-party coverage of one stock or ETF. Official company announcements (deals, partnerships, earnings, launches) are press releases, which this feed omits: pass `include_press_releases: true` or call `press_releases`. For the exact publish time of any row pass its `url` to `article`; for only the 15 newest with times in one request use `feed`.

options.name: asset_class
options.about: Nasdaq asset class of the ticker. `etf` for exchange-traded funds (SPY, QQQ); everything else is `stocks`.

options.name: include_press_releases
options.about: Also fetch the ticker's `press_release` feed (one extra request) and merge its newest `limit` releases into the first page (`offset` 0) as `kind: press_release` rows, ordered newest first with the news by `published_date`; `count` may then exceed `limit`. Deeper pages are news only; `has_more` and `next_offset` follow the news feed. Releases carry no `published_at` (pass their `url` to `article` for it). For every release use `press_releases`.

options.name: limit
options.about: Rows per page (1-100).

options.name: offset
options.about: Rows to skip. Nasdaq serves at most 500 rows per feed and its edge denies deeper offsets, so 490 is the last usable offset; `next_offset` from the previous page is the safe value.

options.name: ticker
options.about: Exchange ticker as Nasdaq spells it (AAPL, BRK.B, SPY). Case-insensitive. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.\-]{0,9}$.

options.name: with_publish_times
options.about: Also fetch the matching RSS feed (one extra request) and copy its pubDate into `published_at` for the stories it lists (the 15 newest). Set false to save the request.

response.about: News stories Nasdaq lists for one ticker (its `articlebysymbol` feed): syndicated articles from Zacks, The Motley Fool, Barchart, RTTNews, Reuters and others, newest first, up to 500 rows deep. Each row carries Nasdaq's calendar day (`published_date`), its server-relative `ago` label, and `published_at` (RFC 3339 UTC) when the story is among the ticker RSS feed's 15 newest. `mentions_ticker` and `primary_symbol_is_ticker` flag how the story relates to the ticker: Nasdaq lists every story that tags the ticker (market wraps and most-active lists naming a dozen symbols included) and files only some under it as primary; keep rows with `primary_symbol_is_ticker` true or a short `related_symbols` for stories about the ticker itself. Company press releases are not in this feed: `include_press_releases: true` merges the ticker's newest releases into the first page (as `kind: press_release`), and `press_releases` pages through all of them. An unknown ticker is `not_found` (Nasdaq itself would answer market-wide news; that fallback is detected and rejected).

fields.name: ago
fields.about: Nasdaq's relative label (`55 minutes ago`, `7 days ago`, or a date for older items) computed on Nasdaq's server at fetch time. It is a different clock from `published_date` and is not a publish time; see `observed_at_ms` for when it was read.

fields.name: description
fields.about: Teaser text; null when empty.

fields.name: id
fields.about: Nasdaq CMS node id; stable per story.

fields.name: kind
fields.about: From the URL family: /articles/, /press-release/, /videos/.

fields.name: mentions_ticker
fields.about: True when the requested ticker is among `related_symbols` or equals `primary_symbol`. Rows where this is false came from Nasdaq's market-wide fallback, not from the ticker's coverage.

fields.name: primary_symbol
fields.about: Nasdaq's `primarysymbol`, upper-cased. Nasdaq fills it only for stories it files under one company; empty for most syndicated market wraps.

fields.name: primary_symbol_is_ticker
fields.about: True when Nasdaq filed the story under the requested ticker (`primary_symbol` equals it). Most ticker-feed rows are syndicated stories that mention the ticker without being primarily about it.

fields.name: primary_topic
fields.about: Topic name from `primarytopic` (Markets, Stocks, Technology...).

fields.name: primary_topic_id
fields.about: Topic term id from `primarytopic`; input for `topic_news`.

fields.name: published_at
fields.about: Publish instant, RFC 3339 UTC, taken from the matching Nasdaq RSS feed item (pubDate) when this story is among that feed's 15 newest items. Null otherwise; `article` returns the instant for any story.

fields.name: published_at_source
fields.about: `rss` when `published_at` came from the RSS feed; null when `published_at` is null.

fields.name: published_date
fields.about: Calendar day from Nasdaq's `created` field (US-Eastern day; the feed carries no time of day). Null when Nasdaq sends none.

fields.name: published_label
fields.about: Nasdaq's `created` text verbatim, e.g. `Sep 21, 2026`.

fields.name: publisher
fields.about: Syndication source as Nasdaq labels it (Zacks, The Motley Fool, Barchart, RTTNews...). Null when Nasdaq sends an empty string (most press releases).

fields.name: related_symbols
fields.about: Every symbol Nasdaq tagged on the story, upper-cased, in Nasdaq's order.

fields.name: url
fields.about: Absolute www.nasdaq.com URL of the story; pass it to `article` for the full text and the exact publish time.
